A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RuCCoD and the same ICD-coding and diagnosis-prediction study. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–H support reliable comparison across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original NER, entity-linking, ICD-coding, and diagnosis-prediction experiments in Sections 4–5 and Appendices C–F, including comparisons of models trained on physician-assigned and automatically linked labels.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports diagnosis-prediction confusion counts and pairwise Jaccard annotation-agreement results.

M1.justification: The NER–entity-linking–code-aggregation pipeline, LoRA/RAG approaches, Longformer diagnosis predictor, and prompts retain the same procedures. Average pooling, Euclidean retrieval, and the selected relabeling pipeline are newly explained rather than established method changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use RuCCoD, RuCCoD-DP, RuCCoN, and NEREL-BIO for the same tasks and transfer scenarios. The new agreement and confusion analyses concern existing data and frequency groups.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same BERT/BINDER, SapBERT, CODER, BERGAMOT, LLM, and Longformer configurations. Comparator membership in the main and appendix tables is unchanged; newly cited methods are not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: V2 adds record–code TP/FP/FN/TN evaluation in Section 5.1 and Jaccard agreement measurement in Appendix A.5. Existing splits, training budgets, and frequency groups remain unchanged. Restriction to test-set codes is newly documented, without establishing that existing experiments were changed or rerun.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and new Table 4 decompose frequent- and rare-code performance into missed, spurious, and correct predictions. Appendix A.5 supplements the existing agreement analysis. Earlier transfer analyses, fine-tuning comparisons, and the I25.2 failure case remain.

E5.justification: Neither version documents repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added Jaccard scores and confusion counts are point metrics, without a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports, for example, bottom-decile false positives of 630 versus 57 for original versus linked training. Appendix A.5 adds Jaccard scores of 0.308, 0.336, and 0.366. Section 3.2 replaces its 50%/74% agreement summary with JSC 0.331. Existing benchmark-table values and result plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2 corrects the false-positive definition: v1 gives FP as St minus Sp, identical to FN; v2 correctly gives Sp minus St. This is a limited mathematical correction, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The introduction corrects the claimed 28% diagnosis-prediction gain from macro-averaged F1 to weighted F1, matching the existing evaluation. The central dataset, benchmarking, transfer-learning, and automatic-relabeling contributions remain.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the added confusion analysis as fewer missed and spurious diagnoses and explicitly reserves final diagnosis for a qualified human. Agreement variability is reframed as expected in Appendix A.5, while the earlier recommendations for standardized annotation protocols or ensemble mitigation disappear.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies average pooling, Euclidean retrieval, the BERT pipeline used for relabeling, and evaluation over test-set codes. V1 promises release upon acceptance; v2 states that code and dataset are available. Appendix hyperparameters, hardware, training times, and prompt content remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction and Appendix B add focused positioning against classification-based and entity-linking ICD work, including Lavergne, Névéol, Coutinho, and Wang. Retrieval references replace the unrelated Liu et al. 2024 sentiment-analysis citation. Most of the related-work survey remains intact.

P1.justification: Several introduction, method, and evaluation paragraphs are rewritten; agreement discussion moves to expanded Appendix A.5. Author affiliations, equal-contribution information, and acknowledgements change. The overall section sequence and most appendix prose remain.

P2.justification: Figure 2 becomes a full-width, two-panel overview with a detailed pipeline example, and Table 4 is added. Existing figures and tables move, and prompt boxes are reformatted and stacked. The other figure images and existing table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves evaluation transparency through confusion counts, additional agreement measurements, and implementation details, while correcting the false-positive formula and headline F1 description. These are useful, limited gains with unchanged benchmark results. Tradeoffs include newly inconsistent task terminology between Appendix B and Section 2 and removal of explicit recommendations for mitigating annotation disagreement.
